scope: Proposition 4.1 (Two-intercept reshaping) of the manuscript “Maximal Multipoint Seshadri Constants in Higher Dimensions” (preprints/Maximal-Multipoint-Seshadri-Constants-in-Higher-Dimensions-October-5-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 039 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dc7a580f2b1d6cf6), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 9-10. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let n ≥ 2, let A, B, a3, . . . , an be positive real numbers, and let (Sk)k≥1 be finite exponent sets satisfying Sk ⊂ k∆(A, B, a3, . . . , an) ∩ Zn , Sk + Sl ⊂ Sk+l (k, l ≥ 1). Set H = AB and d = max(3/A, 2/B). For every real number w > 0 with dw < 1/16, there are finite sets (S′ k)k≥1 such that S′ k ⊂ k∆(w, H/w, a3, . . . , an) ∩ Zn , (4.1) #S′ k = #Sk, S′ k + S′ l ⊂ S′ k+l. (4.2) 9 Moreover, for every k ≥ 1, m ≥ 0, and r ≥ 1, if M(S′ k) surjects onto jets through degree m at some r distinct points of Tn, then M(Sk) does so at some r distinct points of Tn.
